{{recipe}} | [[Cookbook:Cuisine of Mexico|Mexican Cuisine]] | [[Cookbook:Tex-Mex cuisine|Tex-Mex Cuisine]]
==Ingredients==
* 1 [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|tsp]] [[Cookbook:Cayenne Pepper|cayenne pepper]]
* 2 [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|tsp]] [[Cookbook:Salt|salt]]
* 1½ [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tbsp]] [[Cookbook:Chili Powder|chili powder]]
* 3 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tbsp]] white [[Cookbook:Vinegar|vinegar]] (5% acidity)
* 1 can (6 [[Cookbook:Ounce|ounces]]) [[Cookbook:Tomato Paste|tomato paste]]
* ½ [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|tsp]] [[Cookbook:Garlic Powder|granulated garlic]]
* 2¼ [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|tsp]] [[Cookbook:Cornstarch|cornstarch]]
* 3 [[Cookbook:Cup|cups]] water, at room temperature
==Procedure==
#Heat water until [[Cookbook:Boiling|boiling]], then add cornstarch, salt, vinegar, chili powder, garlic, and cayenne pepper.
#Stir until water boils again, then add rest of ingredients.
#Keep stirring until water boils again and the paste breaks up completely.
#Reduce heat and [[Cookbook:Simmering|simmer]] for 20–30 minutes uncovered.
#For short-term storage, refrigerate for no more than 3 days. To store this for longer than 3 days or to store without a refrigerator, pour into 4-[[Cookbook:Ounce|ounce]] mason jars leaving ¼ inch headspace and process for 20 minutes in a boiling water canner.

steps.text: Heat water until boiling, then add cornstarch, salt, vinegar, chili powder, garlic, and cayenne pepper.
Stir until water boils again, then add rest of ingredients.
Keep stirring until water boils again and the paste breaks up completely.
Reduce heat and simmer for 20–30 minutes uncovered.

For short-term storage, refrigerate for no more than 3 days. To store this for longer than 3 days or to store without a refrigerator, pour into 4-ounce mason jars leaving ¼ inch headspace and process for 20 minutes in a boiling water canner.
